conditions: Successfully decoded form body with POST sessionid present
assumptions: Synthetic handler_effect transcribed from cgi-io main_exec; C, not ucode
cgi-io main_exec checks session.access scope=cgi-io object=exec function=read before any command ACL. This oracle stops at that gate.
Successful form-body framing and URL decoding are preconditions; CONTENT_LENGTH/body/URL-decoding failures are outside this slice
This oracle does not parse a command, canonicalize argv0, look up an executable, or fork execv; the exec effect is synthetic from the C gate.
shellquote and basename are not sanitizers. This slice does not treat them, or canonicalize_path, as taint sanitizers.
A cgi-io exec read grant is not a claim that an arbitrary command is authorized
evidence_refs: cgi-io@31cb3c89 main.c main_exec session_access(sid, cgi-io, exec, read)
unknowns: Live cgi-io, uhttpd, and rpcd were not executed; decisions are transcribed from pinned C and ACL JSON.
CONTENT_LENGTH/body framing and URL-decoding failures in postdecode are not modeled; this slice assumes successful form-body decoding.

After the cgi-io exec read gate, main_exec still requires file.exec of the command. The three luci-ssl libexec helpers are modeled by policy:cgi-exec-file-v1. lookup_executable PATH search, execv, and file.exec of other commands are not modeled here.

luci-mod-status-firewall also grants cgi-io exec at luci b2e0be4b; this slice does not staff that fixture login. luci-mod-status-logs and luci-app-package-manager file.exec helpers are policy:cgi-exec-file-v1.
cgi-backup stays on policy:cgi-backup-v1. cgi-upload and cgi-download stay on their own analysis_revisions. dispatcher is not this slice.
